plan_reviews.summary: The plan covers all requirements and is feasible. Design decisions are well-reasoned (IDs not slugs, done+rejected as terminal, impl_stages blocking only). V1 scope is appropriately bounded with clear v2 deferrals.

ideation_cycle_verdicts.reason: Round 4 introduced at least two genuinely new critiques not present in earlier rounds — the override field's lack of an auto-clear policy when blocking dependencies resolve, and the absence of any token-budget strategy for planning prompt dependency context injection — plus a meaningful gap in the poisoning mechanism (impl tasks not covered) and an unresolved UI state for dangling dependencies. These represent substantive new problem space, not mere rewordings of prior points.

Round 8's contributions — eliminating the topological sort as unnecessary given single-feature-per-cycle architecture, dropping the dependency_warning flag due to undefined semantics, and clarifying that no-caching is load-bearing for correctness — are refinements that simplify and validate the round 7 minimal design rather than opening new problem space. The design has stabilized around a concrete, minimal v1 scope with clear deferral boundaries.

Ideation:
Add a `depends_on` field to FeatureFile — a list of immutable 8-char hex IDs referencing other features on the same board. Two module-level functions in state.py handle the core logic: `resolve_dependencies(feature_id, all_features)` returns `{blocked: bool, unresolved_deps: [ids], dangling_deps: [ids]}` and `detect_cycle(feature_id, depends_on, all_features)` prevents circular references. The `_cmd_edit_depends_on` handler validates that proposed dependencies exist on the same board before running cycle detection. JSON persistence is conditional — omit `depends_on` when empty, matching the existing pattern for `done_script`.

Blocking is enforced only in auto-mode's impl_stages pass. A simple `is_blocked(feature_id, resolution_map)` check is added to the existing skip-condition list in server.py alongside retry limits and cooldown — no topological sort is needed because the loop already picks one feature per cycle and breaks, so the natural iteration order already provides implicit fairness across unblocked candidates. Manual moves are always permitted without blocking. Dangling dependencies (IDs that reference no existing feature) are treated as blocking with a log warning; the TUI/WebUI blocked status must display dangling state distinctly so users know action is required. Critically, `resolve_dependencies` must NOT cache results — it must be called fresh inside the broadcast state builder every cycle. This is load-bearing for correctness: when a dependency feature moves to rejected, the next broadcast recomputes blocked status for all dependents automatically.

The discussion went through six rounds of increasing complexity (dependency_events, override tracking, dual dirty-flag caching, plan_invalidation_check, topological sort, poison/cancellation of in-flight tasks) before rounds 6-8 correctly identified this as over-engineering and converged on the minimal design above. Key deferrals for v2: dependency_warning flags (undefined operational semantics — auto-mode treating warnings as skips is functionally equivalent to blocking but with no clear unblocking path), plan_invalidation_check (auto-moving features backward erodes trust; the review stage catches stale plans), override tracking (premature optimization), and dependency_events (history entries suffice for auditability). The self-correcting review cycle handles the main risk — stale plans built on rejected dependencies — without requiring new mechanisms.

The final design adds approximately 150 lines of Python and 20 lines of Go struct changes, fitting cleanly into existing `_cmd_move/_handle_edit` patterns. Implementation detail: the Go FeatureSummary struct needs `DependsOn []string`, `Blocked bool`, and `DanglingDeps []string` fields, with corresponding updates to `_build_golang_state_message()` and WebUI kanban card rendering for three display states: normal, blocked (red lock icon), and dangling (distinct broken-link indicator with tooltip listing missing IDs).

[Ideation concluded by consensus after 8 rounds, 2 cycles.]
